about.title: Stanton Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and it often happens on roads a Stanton family drove every day — Beach Boulevard, Katella Avenue, Cerritos Avenue, or Route 39. Orange County recorded 8 traffic deaths alongside 111 injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, numbers that represent real households now facing funeral costs, lost income, and an absence no settlement can fill. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain other dependents eligible if no closer family exists. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result; we simply connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can explain standing, gather evidence from the crash, and pursue the claim on a contingency basis. That first conversation costs nothing, and it can happen as soon as you're ready.

items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims involving a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Getting connected early helps preserve your family's options.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: A surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children generally have first priority. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may qualify. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm eligibility.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensation for the family, even if criminal charges are also filed against the at-fault driver. The two cases proceed independently and have different standards of proof.

items.question: Does Stanton's crash data affect our claim?
items.answer: Public crash records showing collisions along corridors like Beach Boulevard and Katella Avenue can help establish the circumstances of a crash, but every case turns on its own facts. An independent attorney can request the specific report for your family's incident and build the claim around it.

items.question: How much time do we have to file after a fatal crash?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death, but claims involving a government vehicle or roadway defect can require notice within a much shorter window. Because these deadlines are strict, it's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as your family is able.
